important_uncertainties: Cyprus burial shows close association/taming but does not by itself prove fully modern domestic status.
The grain–rodent–wildcat commensal pathway is strongly supported as a model, not directly observed history.
Egypt contributed strongly to later domestic-cat ancestry/dispersal; avoid reducing this to a clean second independent domestication event.
Ancient mtDNA tracks maternal lineages and should not be described as complete ancestry.
Genome selection signals linked to fear/reward/memory do not establish simple one-gene behavioral causes.
The phrase 'cats domesticated themselves' is useful shorthand but incomplete because humans later transported, tolerated and deliberately bred cats.
